title: Who Sent It or How It Moved? Sender Shortcuts in Cryptocurrency Anti-Money-Laundering Benchmarks, Audited on Elliptic2 and Elliptic++
abstract: arXiv:2611.29744v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Two public benchmarks dominate graph-based anti-money-laundering (AML) research on Bitcoin: the transaction-level Elliptic dataset, extended as Elliptic++, and the subgraph-level Elliptic2. In both, a label is assigned according to the entity that sends the funds. We ask whether models trained on these benchmarks learn how laundering moves or merely who sent the money, and we propose a diagnostic protocol to tell the two apart: a sender lookup baseline, a novelty baseline, a sender-disjoint split with a leakage check, and a decomposition of performance into sender, receiver and intrinsic signal. On Elliptic2 the task largely reduces to classifying the sender. Under the standard random split, a no-learning lookup of sender history reaches a PR-AUC of 0.954, against 0.975 for gradient boosting on 456 features; our reimplementation of RevClassify reproduces its reported 0.97 and falls to 0.126 without sender information. translated_title: 是谁发送的还是如何流动的？在 Elliptic2 与 Elliptic++ 上审计的加密货币反洗钱基准中的“发送者捷径”问题
translated_abstract: 两个公开基准主导了基于图的比特币反洗钱（AML）研究：交易级的 Elliptic 数据集（其扩展版本为 Elliptic++）以及子图级的 Elliptic2。在这两个基准中，标签都是根据发送资金的实体来分配的。我们提出这样一个问题：在这些基准上训练的模型，学到的究竟是洗钱资金如何流动，还是仅仅学到了是谁发送了资金？为此，我们提出了一套诊断协议来区分二者，包括：发送者历史查表基线、新颖性基线、带泄漏检查的发送者不相交数据划分，以及将模型性能分解为发送者信号、接收者信号和内在信号的分析。在 Elliptic2 上，该任务在很大程度上可简化为对发送者进行分类。在标准随机划分下，一个无需学习的发送者历史查表方法即可达到 0.954 的 PR-AUC，而在 456 个特征上使用梯度提升方法可达到 0.975；我们对 RevClassify 的重新实现复现了其报告的 0.97，但在去除发送者信息后性能降至 0.126。当发送者……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出一套诊断协议，揭示 Elliptic2 和 Elliptic++ 反洗钱基准的标签主要由资金发送者决定，模型实际学到的是“发送者是谁”的捷径而非洗钱资金如何流动的内在模式。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a diagnostic protocol showing that labels in the Elliptic2 and Elliptic++ AML benchmarks are largely determined by the sender, meaning models learn a sender shortcut—who sent the funds—rather than the intrinsic patterns of how laundering actually moves.
